mathematical_semantics: every load-bearing actor/procedure/artifact identity on an authority path is a lowercase SHA-256 content digest; human display labels are inadmissible even in fields named *_hash (the local naming attack); binding is transitive over the receipt chain, so changing any judged element invalidates the receipt

the digest-to-external-world mapping is the declared trust root established by the external acquisition/review process; recursing past it would self-certify what the design refuses to self-certify; stricter binding layers narrow earlier admissions and never promote earlier rejections

verification_contracts: four bindings for every evidence-bearing receipt: current-proposer binding (no cross-proposer reuse), subject-pair binding (digest of the informal/formal pair), complete-dossier binding (cutoff, corpus, routes, fingerprint, manifest, matches - any post-review flip invalidates), and independent attestation (separate attestor identity; self-attestation fails closed)

failure_signatures: failure:ABSORB.EVIDENCE_BIND.v0:naming-attack - a display label in a hash-named field reaches the authority path
failure:ABSORB.EVIDENCE_BIND.v0:receipt-reuse - a receipt survives across proposers or supersession
failure:ABSORB.EVIDENCE_BIND.v0:dossier-flip - a judged element changes after review while the receipt stays valid
falsifiers: construct a receipt chain in which one judged element's bytes change and the chain still validates; a single such case refutes the binding layer
